full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 18 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Betagi, Barguna against the opposite parties as defendants for declaration of title in the suit land and also for a declaration that the order dated 30-1-1997 passed in Case No. 2 Ba/95-96 by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Betagi is illegal, collusive, without jurisdiction, null and void stating, inter-alia, that the suit land mentioned in "Kha" schedule to the plaint appertaining to SA Khatian Nos. 346 and 347 originally belonged to one Amir Uddin Sarang, who died leaving two sons namely, Golam Mostafa and Golam Moula and daughter Aklima Khatun. Among the aforesaid heirs of Amir Uddin, Golam Moula died leaving behind only son defendant No. 5, Nazrul Islam @ Zinnah, Aklima Khatun died leaving four sons, the defendant Nos. 6-8 and one Shahidullah and three daughters, the defendant Nos. 9-11. The said Shahidullah died leaving defendant Nos. 12-15, Golam Mustafa died leaving defendant Nos. 17-25. 

 3. According to Muslim Law of Inheritance defendant No. 5, Md. Nazrul Islam @ Zinnah and defendant No. 6 Abdus Samad got 0.1¾ decimal and 0.0012 decimals of land in SA Khatian Nos. 346 and 347 respectively. They also acquired 0.0012 acres in Khatian No. 348. They transferred an area of 0.02¼ decimals of land to the plaintiff by a registered deed of sale dated 15-1-1994 and handed over possession. The defendant Nos. 9-12 sold .004½ decimals of land and 0.1½ decimals of land by two registered deeds dated 18-5-1994 and 9-8-1994 to the plaintiff. Thus, the plaintiff acquired 0.0180 acres and 0.0015 acres of land under SA Khatian Nos. 346 and 347 respectively and has possessed the same by purchase. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 showing Golam Mustafa as the only heir of Amir Uddin Sarang created some fraudulent and collusive sale deeds in the name of different persons with an intention to gain the property illegally and also managed to get their names mutated in the khatian. The plaintiff on coming to know about the said mutation filed an application before the defendant No. 3 under section 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for mutation of his name. Accordingly, the defendant No. 3 by his order dated 10-9-1995 partly modified the mutation by including the name of the petitioner in SA Khatian Nos. 346 and 347 to the extent of 9 annas 12 gandas share. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 against the said order filed a revision before the defendant No. 4 who after hearing, by its order dated 15-5-1996 cancelled the order dated 10-9-1995 passed by the defendant No. 3 and directed to ascertain the disputed plot and the number of heirs of Amir Uddin Sarang. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 managed to obtain a false certificate from the Chairman of Naria Union Parishad and filed the same before the defendant No. 3 and managed to get an order dated 30-1-1997 illegally in their favour, hence the present suit. 

 5. The defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing a written statement. Later on, the defendant No. 1 by filing a petition adopted the said written statement filed by defendant No. 2. They denied all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable, barred by limitation, bed for defect of parties and no cause of action for the suit. Further case of the defendants is that the original owner Amir Uddin Sarang died leaving only son Mohammad Golam Mustafa and he had no son named Golam Moula and daughter Aklima Khatun. Golam Mustafa was only heir of Amir Uddin Sarang, who transferred the entire suit property to one Wares Ali Howlader by a registered deed dated 21-12-1963. Wares Ali sold 0.0025 acres to one Abdul Latif Sikder by a registered deed dated 5-6-1964. Said Wares Ali again sold 0.01 satak of land to one Habul Krishna Das and on the same day he also sold 0.1/2 decimal of land to Protima Rani Das. On 27-9-1988 Wares Ali again sold 0.1/2 decimal to one Depok Kumar Das. The aforesaid Abdul Latif Sikder sold her purchased land to one Dilruba by a registered deed dated 26-4-1988. After purchase in the manner aforesaid Habul Kumar Das, Protima Rani Das, Dipok Kumar Das and Dilruba got their names mutated in the Khatian vide Mutation Case Nos. 23/89-90 and 776/79-80. While Habul Krishna Das and others were in possession of the land, they jointly sold .03 decimals by two registered deed dated 25-5-1991 to defendant No. 1 and delivered possession of the same. On the same day Dilruba sold 0.0025 acres of land to the defendant No. 2 who after purchase got his name mutated in the khatian by Mutation Case No. 64/93-94. In this way, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 acquired the entire land of SA Khatian Nos. 346 and 347 along with the structures standing thereon and has been possessing the same, but the plaintiff in order to grab the property illegally showing the defendant Nos. 5-16 as the imaginary heirs of late Amir Uddin Sareng managed to get two sale deeds dated 15-1-1994 and 18-5-1994 by false personation and on the basis of the said fraudulent kabalas filed petition against the mutation before the defendant No. 3 and having failed in his attempt filed the present suit. 

 7. Mr Mohammad Eunus, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner submits that the appellate court while allowing the appeal has not considered the evidences of the plaintiff-petitioner both oral and documentary. He also submits that the appellate court did not consider the Exhibit-8 series Khatian No. 207 wherein some non-suited plots of land was recorded in the names of Golam Mustafa and Golam Moula son of Haji Amir Hossain. While the appellate court dismissing the appeal it failed to notice that the said Exhibits stand in the names Golam Mustafa and Golam Moula. Therefore, it amply proves that Amir Uddin Sarang had two sons. It is also argued that the sale deed in the name of Waresh Ali dated 21-12-1963 in its schedule No. 1 contain Plot No. 363 but the defendant made it into plot No. 366 by interpolation and, as such, the defendant acquired no right, title and possession in plot No. 366 by way of successive transfer from Waresh Ali. 

 9. Mr Gazi Md Mohsin with Ms Dilshad Niazi Manna, the learned Advocates appearing for the opposite parties submit that the plaintiff failed to prove by adducing and or producing any evidence both oral and documentary that Amir Uddin had two sons and one daughter. The defendant by submitting a heir ship certificate duly issued by the local Chairman could able to prove that Amir Uddin died leaving only son Golam Mostafa Sarang. Therefore, the appellate court by allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment of the trial court has not committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that the documents filed by the petitioner have not in any way proved that Amir Uddin Sarang died leaving two sons and one daughter. The appellate court considered all the evidences on record and found that the petitioner could not prove their case beyond doubt, particularly, the number of heirs of Amir Uddin Sarang. It is also argued that the heir of Amir Uddin Sarang, Golam Mustafa had transferred the suit property to one Waresh Ali in the year 1963 i.e. before 34 years of filing of the suit. Had there been any other heirs of Amir Uddin other than Golam Mustafa as alleged by the plaintiff why they did not claim the property as co-sharer for a long period of 32 years. The plaintiff could not satisfy such fact before the appellate court. Mr Mohsin further submits that even if, we take the fact of containing plot No. 363 in the deed dated 21-12-1963 to be true in that case also title of the defendant cannot be questioned as the Khatian No. 346 contain only plot No. 366. In this situation, in the absence of any other plot in Khatian No. 346 it should be construed that the predecessor of the defendants, Waresh Ali purchased the land of plot No. 366 under Khatian No. 346. He further submits that Exhibit-8 series submitted by the petitioner has not been proved in accordance with the law to prove that Amir Uddin had two sons, named Golam Mustafa and Golam Moula and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 13. From a perusal of the aforesaid three Exhibits, it appears that in the schedule of the aforesaid deeds, no boundary of the property sold has been given and in which portion of the plot they were delivered possession has not been mentioned. Admittedly, the plaintiff has alleged to have purchased certain quantum of land covered by plot Nos. 366 and 442. In the situation, without any specification of the property in the deed the plaintiff at best may be considered as a co-sharer in the property and, as such, mere declaration of title without specification of the property is not maintainable. The plaintiff also could not satisfy the court why the three certificates dated 23-1-1994 issued by the Chairman of Naria Union Parisand was given on white paper. The appellate court found that those certificates as Exhibit-4 have not been proved in accordance with the law of evidence and, as such, by the said certificates, claim of the plaintiff as to number of heirs of Amir Uddin Sarang has not been established. Exhibit- 8 series also not relating to the suit property but relating to non-suited property wherein the name of original owner has been mentioned as Haji Amir Hossain not Amir Uddin Sarang as appearing in the suit khatian Nos. 346 and 347. For that reasons also it cannot be conclusively considered that those persons are the same person. The trial court in its judgment considered those documents and found that Amir Uddin Sarang and Haji Amir Hossain is the same person without any corroborating evidences to that effect. The trial court though observed that the plaintiff could able to prove that Amir Uddin had two sons and one daughter and found that the plaintiffs are owner of a portion of the suit property but failed to observe that in the absence of any specification of the property a suit for simple declaration without partition is not maintainable. 

 15. From perusal of Khatian No. 346 it appears that it contain only plot No. 366. In the schedule to the deed dated 21-12-1963 Khatain number and quantum of land correctly written but plot number has been written as 363 in place of 366. In this situation, I am of the opinion that in the absence of any other plot in Khatain No. 346 it should be construed that Waresh Ali purchased the land of plot No. 366 under Khatian No. 346 and, as such, for the aforesaid wrong, title of Waresh Ali cannot be construed as defective.
